name: manual_fb4175
claim: When a bash script under test resolves its own location via ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}/SCRIPT_DIR for self-referential logic (e.g. 'am I the canonical checkout'), a pytest fixture that spoofs cwd while invoking the real, on-disk script file does NOT exercise the 'invoked from a different checkout' scenario — SCRIPT_DIR always resolves to where the file physically lives, regardless of subprocess cwd. To test that logic in isolation, copy the actual script (plus its sourced dependencies) into the synthetic fixture directory and invoke that copy.

decisions.notes: First attempt at testing check-guard-sync-divergence.sh's canonical-root auto-resolution spoofed cwd via subprocess.run(cwd=downstream) while invoking the real module-level CHECKER path — CANON_ROOT kept resolving to the real orama-system worktree (crawling real sibling directories like /private<local-tmp-file> instead of the synthetic tmp_path fixture), producing baffling 'ambiguous orama-system roots' errors that were actually correct behavior operating on the wrong (real) filesystem scope. Fixed by writing a _plant_checker_copy() helper that copies the checker script + guard-sync-manifest.sh + resolve_sibling_git_repo.sh into the fixture and invoking that copy. orama-system PR 311, ECC push-gate analysis 2026-08-14.
